## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

In this tree, the PM operations are defined in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1715-1753`

Only two PM-operation entries point to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
System suspend:
  PM core
    └─ i915_pm_ops.suspend
         └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
              ├─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
              ├─ if (!i915) return -ENODEV
              ├─ if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
              │    return 0
              └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                   └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
                        └─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
                           └─ display suspend/state capture
```

Relevant source:

- Callback registration: `i915_driver.c:1719`
- `i915_pm_suspend()`: `i915_driver.c:1392-1404`
- `i915_drm_suspend()`: `i915_driver.c:1103-1145`
- Display suspend: `intel_display_driver.c:684-709`

Hibernate poweroff uses the same function pointer:

```text
Hibernate:
  PM core
    └─ i915_pm_ops.poweroff
         └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
              └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                   └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Registration:

```c
.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend,
```

at `i915_driver.c:1745`.

Therefore, the complete set of PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend` is:

| PM callback | Function target | Reaches `i915_pm_suspend`? |
|---|---|---:|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend` | Yes |
| `.poweroff` | `i915_pm_suspend` | Yes |
| `.prepare` | `i915_pm_prepare` | No |
| `.suspend_late` | `i915_pm_suspend_late` | No |
| `.suspend_noirq` | `i915_pm_suspend_noirq` | No |
| `.freeze` | `i915_pm_freeze` | No; calls `i915_drm_suspend` directly |
| `.poweroff_late` | `i915_pm_poweroff_late` | No |
| `.poweroff_noirq` | `i915_pm_poweroff_noirq` | No |
| `.runtime_suspend` | `intel_runtime_suspend` | No |
| resume/thaw/restore callbacks | resume functions | No |

`i915_pm_freeze()` is a related path:

```text
i915_pm_freeze(kdev)
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

It bypasses `i915_pm_suspend`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in this source tree. The runtime PM callback is named:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

at `i915_driver.c:1752`.

Thus, none of the callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

The runtime-suspend path is separate:

```text
PM core
  └─ i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
       └─ intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
            ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
            ├─ intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
            ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore)
            └─ intel_display_power_suspend(display)
```

It does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()` or `i915_drm_suspend()`.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The current display function is named `intel_display_driver_suspend()`, not `intel_display_suspend()`.

```text
PM callback argument
  kdev: struct device *
    │
    └─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)
         └─ dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
              └─ drm: struct drm_device *
                   └─ to_i915(drm)
                        └─ container_of(drm,
                                       struct drm_i915_private,
                                       drm)
                             └─ i915 / dev_priv
```

The exact conversion is in `i915_drv.h:328-332`:

```c
static inline struct drm_i915_private *kdev_to_i915(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_device *drm = dev_get_drvdata(kdev);

	return drm ? to_i915(drm) : NULL;
}
```

Then the suspend path propagates the object as follows:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  └─ struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  ├─ struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
  ├─ struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display
  └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Inside `intel_display_driver_suspend()`:

```text
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
  ├─ if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
  │    return 0
  ├─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
  ├─ display->restore.modeset_state = state
  ├─ flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)
  └─ intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
```

Important detail: `dev_priv` is not passed directly to the display layer. It is converted to the embedded `drm` object, converted back in `i915_drm_suspend()`, and then reduced to `dev_priv->display`. From that point onward, the display suspend code carries only the `struct intel_display *display` pointer.
